sections.h2: Who sends the Murfreesboro tax bill
sections.html:
A Murfreesboro owner pays two separate collectors. The Rutherford County Property Assessor appraises each parcel and produces the notices. The county's own share goes to the Rutherford County Trustee, and the City of Murfreesboro Finance and Tax department collects the city share.

  • Assessor's office: 319 N. Maple Street, Suite 200, Murfreesboro, TN 37130, phone (615) 898-7750. Call for billing questions or to fix a mailing address.
  • City Finance Department: City Hall, 111 W. Vine St., first floor, phone (615) 893-5210, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • County Trustee: Historic Courthouse on the Public Square, phone (615) 898-7705.

The city applies its own rate to the county's assessed value. The county mails the bills and the city collects its portion. The city's property tax page lays out the process.

sections.h2: The Murfreesboro market and what it means for taxes
sections.html:
Murfreesboro is the seat of Rutherford County, about 34 miles southeast of downtown Nashville in Middle Tennessee. The 2020 census counted 152,769 people, and the July 2025 estimate is 171,178, an increase of 12.0%. The median owner-occupied home is worth $402,100, compared with $382,600 for the county, and owners live in 52.4% of homes. Median household income is $80,108 and median gross rent is $1,481.

At a median value above $400,000, the tax is a meaningful line on a settlement statement. Know the exact amount owed before you set a price.

sections.h2: What the 2026 reappraisal means for your bill
sections.html:
Tennessee requires a countywide reappraisal every four years, and Rutherford County's last cycle before this one was 2022. Between cycles, values hold steady except for new construction, additions, demolition or corrections.

A higher appraisal does not automatically raise the tax. Under the state's certified tax rate law, a city or county must hold public hearings before it adopts a rate that collects more in total than the year before. The County Commission sets the rate, not the Assessor. A lender's appraisal can also differ from the Assessor's figure, since a lender studies one house in more depth than a mass appraisal can.

The math is simple. Take the appraised value and multiply by 25 percent for residential property, 30 percent for business personal property or 40 percent for commercial. Divide by 100, then multiply by the rate. The county rate was $1.8762 per $100 for 2025. Because 2026 was a reappraisal year, ask the Trustee or the city for the rate on your current bill and do not reuse an old figure.

sections.h2: When is Murfreesboro city property tax due?
sections.html:
The city's 2026 bills can be paid from October 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 without interest. Starting March 1, 2027, unpaid base tax picks up 1.5 percent per month or any part of a month.

Murfreesboro city property tax dates and costs for 2026 bills

The online portal is murfreesborotntax.com. The city takes cash, check or card, though bank counter checks and two-party checks are refused, and partial payments are fine. The county bill runs on its own schedule. It is due the first Monday of October, can be paid until the last day of February without interest, and carries no early payment discount.

sections.h2: How to appeal a Rutherford County valuation
sections.html:
Start with a call or visit to the Assessor at (615) 898-7750, where an appraiser goes over the property record with you. Wrong square footage or a listed defect are the usual topics at this informal stage.

If that does not settle it, the next stop is a hearing before the Rutherford County Board of Equalization. Appointments open in the first week of May, and hearings normally run in June. Skipping the county board makes the assessment final with no further appeal, so do not bypass it.

After the county board comes the State Board of Equalization. It starts with an administrative law judge, and the appellant pays a state fee. The last step is a suit in Davidson County Chancery Court. An appeal does not delay the bill, so pay on time and ask for any refund afterward.

Tennessee offers relief to homeowners 65 and over, to disabled homeowners, and to disabled veteran owners and their surviving spouses. The relief program is offered by both the City of Murfreesboro and Rutherford County, so an eligible owner files with both to cover both bills. The filing deadline is 35 days after the city's delinquency date.

For veteran households, the surviving spouse must have been married to the veteran at death and must not have remarried, and the property must be the applicant's primary residence. The most market value counted in the calculation is the first $175,000. Apply at the Trustee, (615) 898-7705, or the city tax office, (615) 893-5210.

Murfreesboro and Rutherford County have also approved the constitutional tax freeze for owners 65 and older. Contact the Trustee for forms. State relief does not erase the bill. It only reimburses tax you have already paid.

sections.h2: How to settle Murfreesboro property tax when you sell
sections.html:
New owners are told to read the closing statement or ask the title company who pays the year's tax, and unpaid tax continues to accrue against the property. Check both the city and county balances. The city portion is billed separately from the county's.

  1. Phone the City Finance Department and the Trustee for current balances.
  2. If an old year is delinquent, ask the Rutherford County Chancery Court clerk for a payoff figure, because costs and interest change it. Delinquent real property tax can also be paid online through the court's services, which list delinquent amounts.
  3. Tell the title company about each office that holds a balance.
  4. Have every balance paid from your proceeds at closing.

That sequence works the same for a vacant or inherited house with an overdue bill. A buyer who pays cash and closes as-is can move quickly once the payoffs are confirmed in writing.

faqs.q: When is Murfreesboro city property tax due for 2026?
faqs.a: February 28, 2027 is the last day without interest. Payment opened October 1, 2026, and interest of 1.5 percent a month starts March 1, 2027.

faqs.q: Who do I call with a question about my Murfreesboro tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Rutherford County Assessor at (615) 898-7750 for billing and address changes. The City Tax Department at (615) 893-5210 handles payments and relief programs.

faqs.q: Did Murfreesboro property values change in 2026?
faqs.a: Yes. 2026 was a countywide reappraisal year in Rutherford County, following 2022. Higher values do not necessarily mean a higher bill under the certified rate rules, so check the rate on your notice.

faqs.q: Can seniors get a break on Murfreesboro property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. State relief covers qualifying owners 65 and older, disabled owners and disabled veteran owners. The city and county have also approved a tax freeze for owners 65 and over.

faqs.q: How do I pay Murfreesboro property tax online?
faqs.a: Use murfreesborotntax.com with a card or e-check. The processor adds about 2.5 percent plus $0.30 for cards or $1.50 for an e-check. The county portion is paid separately through the Trustee.
